q1_issues.issue: The entire that-clause complement ("that nobody goes in there") is dropped, so the sealed directive records only that a making-sure was commanded and nothing whatever about what was to be ensured.

q2_gaps: a directive/ensure verb with a finite that-clause complement — "make sure that P" is not one of the listed propositional-attitude verbs and the imperative section says nothing about how a clausal complement attaches inside the Directive seal

a wholly negative sealed proposition — the registered no-polarity-carrier-inside-a-seal limitation leaves "nobody goes in there" with no expressible form at all under Directive, and no rule says what to emit in that case
a bare quantificational pronoun ("nobody") — the quantifier machinery covers "no N" / "none of the Ns" determiners but never states the implicit domain kind such a pronoun ranges over
a deictic locative ("in there") — deictic TIMES are speech-anchored constants, but deictic places are never addressed
a verb + adjectival-complement fixed expression ("make sure") — no rule says whether it fuses into one surface symbol, decomposes as a resultative (make + sure), or is a control/attitude verb
notes: Nothing asserted here is false — the Directive shell and the strength/confidence are right — but the parse is near-empty relative to the sentence. Dropping the complement may be partly forced by the seal-polarity limitation, yet even the locative and the commanded proposition's participants leave no trace.
